title: Synthetic, Multi-Layer, Self-Oscillating Vocal Fold Model Fabrication
protocol: Create solid models of three vocal fold layers: superficial lamina propria, ligament, and body layers using 3D computer-aided design (CAD).
Export CAD models as stereolithography (STL) files.
Send STL files to a custom machine shop for rapid prototyping.
Create a box-shaped mold form using thin pieces of acrylic material.
Approximate dimensions are 2.54 cm high × 5.72 cm wide × 6.35 cm deep.
Adhere the bottom of the form to a flat acrylic plate.
Seal all interior edges with vacuum grease.
Place a small amount of vacuum grease on the lateral side of the solid model.
Press the model into the bottom of the mold form cavity, vacuum grease side down.
Coat the mold form and solid model liberally with release agent.
Ensure the release agent reaches into all corners of the mold form cavity using a paint brush.
Mix 10 parts A and one part B of Smooth-Sil 950 platinum silicone rubber by weight in a container.
Place mold form with uncured silicone rubber in a vacuum chamber and reduce pressure to around 26 inches Hg below atmospheric pressure for approximately three minutes.
Remove degassed silicone from the chamber and pour into the mold form cavity.
Place the mold with uncured silicone back into the vacuum chamber and degas again.
Remove from the vacuum chamber and place on a level surface.
Allow to cure for 24 hours before removing the mold from the mold form.
Repeat steps 1.1 through 1.4 to create molds for each of the superficial lamina propria, ligament, and body layers.
Cut ligament layer mold at the center of the medial surface in the anterior-posterior direction with a straight razor.
Apply thin layer of release agent to body mold cavity with paint brush.
Mix one part B and one part A of Ecoflex 00-30 Supersoft Platinum Silicone by weight.
Add one part Silicone Thinner by weight to reduce the eventual cured stiffness of the material.
Mix together for 30 seconds and place in vacuum chamber for one minute to remove entrapped air.
Remove mixture from vacuum and pour into the body mold cavity, but do not fill to the top of the entire mold cavity.
Place in oven at 250 °F for 30 minutes.
Remove from oven and cool.
Mix one part B and one part A of Dragon Skin by weight.
Add one part Silicone Thinner by weight.
Mix vigorously for 30 seconds, place in vacuum for 1 minute.
Pour into the body mold cavity until full.
Place in oven at 250 °F for 30 minutes.
Remove mold from oven and cool.
Remove model from mold.
Allow to cool to room temperature.
Remove any release agent on the surface of the body layer with paper towel.
Apply thin layer of release agent on ligament mold cavity surface with paint brush.
Place a 30 cm thread in the mold by pushing it into the cut from the straight razor.
Thoroughly mix one part B and one part A of Ecoflex 00-30 and four parts of Silicone Thinner (by weight).
Place mixture in vacuum chamber to remove air bubbles.
Pour mixture into ligament mold cavity.
Press body-backing model into the ligament mold cavity, starting from one side and moving gently to the other.
If air bubbles are present, remove model from mold cavity, refill with uncured silicone, and repeat pressing model into the mold.
Place mold in oven for 30 minutes.
Remove mold from oven and cool to room temperature.
Remove model from mold.
Remove excess release agent with paper towel.
Apply a thin layer of release agent on the superficial lamina propria (SLP) mold cavity surface with a paint brush.
Mix one part component B, one part component A of Ecoflex 00-30, and eight parts silicone thinner by weight.
Vacuum as done previously and pour into SLP mold cavity.
Insert the ligament-body-backing model into the superficial lamina propria mold cavity using the process described in Step 2.1.4.
Place the mold in an oven at 250 °F and cure for one hour.
Remove from oven and allow to cool.
Remove the model slowly and with extreme care so that the superficial lamina propria remains intact.
Place the vocal fold model on a flat surface with the backing down.
Remove support material with a straight razor.
Suspend threads in air by attaching them to an object of greater height than the model.
Mix one part component B, one part component A of Dragon Skin with one part silicone thinner.
Vacuum and pour over the model.
Allow to cure for one hour.
Repeat the process to create a thicker layer.
Remove excess material with a straight razor.
Apply a thin layer of silicone glue on the back and side surfaces of each completed vocal fold model.
Insert the model into a recessed cut of an acrylic mounting plate.
Align the model medial surface with the top of the acrylic plate.
Wipe away excess glue.
Allow glue to cure for one hour.
Apply talc powder to the model surface to reduce tackiness.
Mark dots on the model medial surface using a fine-point Sharpie pen after applying talc powder.
Place long bolts through holes of the mounting plate with threaded ends pointing toward the model.
Lay threads over the bolts.
Put closed cell foam over the bolts to close any air gaps.
Pair this prepared model with another vocal fold model that has been similarly mounted to an acrylic holder.
Tighten screws to compress the foam and bring the medial surfaces together until the desired pre-vibratory gap is reached.
Ensure both sets of threads are placed over the bolts and extend outward from the acrylic plates in the anterior-posterior direction.
Mount vocal fold pair on air supply tube.
Tie the anterior threads together to form a loop.
Repeat for the posterior threads.
Hang desired weight on the loops simultaneously.
Models are now ready for testing and data collection.
